_about: Parameters for the real-area instance (Nagasandra + Dodda Bidarakallu). Every value has a label: OBSERVED (from a dataset), SOURCED (from a published document, see 'source'), DERIVED (computed from other values), ASSUMED (our choice, must be sensitivity-tested or replaced).

n_points_total.label: ASSUMED
n_points_total.note: Within the agreed 40-80 range. Split between wards in proportion to ward population (TOT_P). Sensitivity: 40 and 80.

collection_road_types.label: ASSUMED
collection_road_types.note: Door-to-door collection happens on streets with house frontage. Excluded: motorway, trunk and their links (NH-48/Tumkur Road, NICE Road) - vehicles travel on them but do not collect there.

speed_kmph_by_road_type.label: ASSUMED
speed_kmph_by_road_type.note: Base (no-surprise) morning speed of a loaded collection vehicle. Only 84 of 14,837 OSM edges have maxspeed, and posted limits are not travel speeds. Sanity anchor: TomTom Traffic Index 2025, Bengaluru: city average 16.6 km/h, morning rush 14.6 km/h, free-flow ~29 km/h (2 min 4 s per km). TO BE REPLACED by calibration (scripts/calibrate_travel_times.py).

time_origin.label: SOURCED
time_origin.source: BBMP/BSWML service-provider scope (OpenCity): door-to-door collection from households to begin no later than 6:30 AM.
time_origin.note: BBMP (Aug 2025) fixed auto-tipper mustering at 5:30-6:30 am (previously 6:00-7:30), so collection starts ~06:30. Deccan Herald reports door-to-door from ~7:30 in practice -> modelled as a random start delay (see uncertainty).

household_window_min.label: SOURCED
household_window_min.source: Same scope document: commercial collection to begin preferably at 11:00 AM, after households are done. So households = 06:30-11:00 = minutes 0-270.
household_window_min.note: On time = service starts by 11:00. This is the contractual window, not a citizen-promised slot.

household_size.label: DERIVED (Census 2011)
household_size.source: Census 2011 households and population of the four old BBMP wards that cover the study area (14 Bagalagunte 17,117 HH / 65,113; 15 T. Dasarahalli 8,849 / 33,042; 39 Chokkasandra 16,537 / 59,289; 40 Dodda Bidarakallu 19,506 / 72,794): 230,238 / 62,009 = 3.71 persons per household. Table: Wikipedia 'List of wards in Bangalore (2009-2023)', citing BBMP ward data.
household_size.note: Cross-check against Census 2011 Primary Census Abstract if the guide asks.

vehicle_capacity_households.label: SOURCED
vehicle_capacity_households.source: BPAC roundtable (BBMP data): one auto tipper per 1000 households. OpenCity BBMP SWM doc: one per 750-household block. Sensitivity: 750.
vehicle_capacity_households.note: BBMP Time & Motion Study (2015, BBMP + KUIDFC/iDeCK): auto tipper 500 kg (475 kg wet + 25 kg sanitary drum). Microplan 2017: one auto tipper per 750-household block. We keep 1000 HH as the per-shift workload norm; 750 is a sensitivity case.

service_min_per_household.label: ASSUMED
service_min_per_household.note: Implied ceiling from the norms: 270 min / 1000 HH = 0.27 min per HH including driving inside the street segment. 0.2 leaves ~25% of the shift for travel between points. Replace with field timing if the team can observe one auto tipper.

population_field.label: OBSERVED
population_field.note: Appears to be Census-2011-based, so absolute counts are likely below today's. Only the SPLIT of demand between points and wards depends on it if we size the fleet from the same numbers; absolute load is a known limitation.

depot.label: MISSING
depot.note: Auto-tipper mustering point for these wards. Fill data/raw/facilities.json (see data/raw/facilities_TEMPLATE.json). Until then a clearly-labelled PLACEHOLDER is used for pipeline tests only - no results may be reported from it.

random_seed.label: ASSUMED
random_seed.note: k-means seed for reproducible point placement

fleet_extra.label: DERIVED (team to confirm)
fleet_extra.note: Fleet AVAILABLE = ceil(households / capacity) + fleet_extra. With the norm alone (13 x 1000 HH for 12,686 HH = 97.6% full) OR-Tools found no plan in 60 s from scratch (packing is hard; time is NOT binding - 9 trucks suffice without the capacity limit). With 14 available, the best plan found (120 s) uses only 13 trucks, i.e. the norm IS feasible. So +1 is search room, not a bigger fleet. Alternative to discuss: multi-trip auto tippers (needs the transfer point).

traffic.label: ASSUMED (no public Bengaluru data on day-to-day variability)
traffic.note: Ward sigmas deliberately EQUAL so any ward gap comes from geography/plans, not from our assumption. Intensity x2 tested.

uncertainty.label: ASSUMED, bounded by sources; full sensitivity grid reported
uncertainty.note: start delay ~ Uniform(0,U): U=60 spans the gap between the contractual 06:30 start and the ~07:30 start reported by Deccan Herald. Service-time CVs: no public Bengaluru time-and-motion variability figures; waste-collection GPS studies report positively skewed, highly variable service/facility times. Grid: U in {30,60,90}, CV x{0.5,1,1.5}.

slot_width_min.label: ASSUMED
slot_width_min.note: Published collection slot width. Sensitivity 30 and 90.
